newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Ciba boosts production in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Ciba boosts production in Hungary.

text.p: Hungary's Humanpharma Kft and Switzerland's Ciba-Geigy AG will boost their cooperation in Hungary and Ciba will now have two important drugs manufactured in Hungary, company officials said.

"The total supply for the Hungarian market of the antiphlogistic (anti-inflammatory) drug Voltaren 75 and the pain killer Cataflam 50 mg will be produced in Godollo (Humanpharma's headquarters)," the two partners said in a joint statement on Wednesday.
The agreement was signed last year by Ciba Hungaria Kft, the Hungarian unit of Ciba-Geigy AG and Humanpharma, a member of Human Oltoanyagtermelo es Gyogyszergyarto Rt group.
The launch of the local production of the two drugs continues the traditional production cooperation between Ciba and Hungaropharma.
"We have already some experience of working with Humanpharma...one product is already produced," Gary Phillips, managing director of Ciba Hungaria, told a news conference.
"That gave us confidence to offer them the opportunity to produce these two other products."
In addition to the manufacturing of antidepressant Ludiomil, Humanpharma will produce 1.8 million boxes of Voltaren 75 and six million boxes of Cataflam 50 mg until the year 2000, the statement said.
The costs of the launch of the production amount to 150 million forints, fully paid by Humanpharma.
Ciba cooperates with other pharmaceuticals in Hungary, too, including Biogal, Hungarian unit of Israel's Teva and Chinoin, unit of French drugs and cosmetics company Sanofi, member of Elf Aquitaine.

Phillips said Ciba Hungaria expects a turnover of nine billion forints in 1996. Ciba Hungaria's pharma division generated sales of 3.1 billion forints in 1995 which it expects to boost by around 10 percent this year, he said.
Ciba and another Swiss pharmaceuticals company, Sandoz AG announced their merger, to form Novartis AG, in early March and the step was approved by shareholders of both companies in April.
